highlights.title: Rangers miss chance to go top as Jones earns Dundee a point
highlights.summary: Callum Jones scored a second-half equaliser as Rangers were held to a 2-2 draw by Dundee and missed the chance to go top of the Scottish Premiership.
body: Dundee opened the scoring when Rangers failed to deal with a routine long ball, with Bradley Fink capitalising to round the goalkeeper and slide home.
The lead did not last long, though, as Badredine Bouanani cut inside and curled in a stunning equaliser to open his account for Rangers.
Nico Raskin scored the goal of the game when his shot from outside the area went in off the underside of the crossbar.
But Jones then caught Dan Neil dwelling on the ball and nicked it off the Rangers captain to slot home the Dundee equaliser.

highlights.title: Supercell brings Clash Royale to tabletop with new Kickstarter board game
highlights.summary: Supercell is bringing Clash Royale to the tabletop with Clash Royale: The Grand Arena, a board game developed with Maestro Media, set to launch on Kickstarter on October 20, 2026.
body: Designed by David Gordon, Ryan Rodriguez, and TAM, the game supports two to four players who can deploy cards, attack opponents and send their towers across two lanes.
Players will compete to destroy towers and collect crowns, the player holding the most crowns in the end wins.

The tabletop adaptation aims to retain several mechanics from the mobile game, including card-based strategy. Players build eight-card decks around a chosen champion, whose evolution card remains with them throughout the game. Players can upgrade or add characters to their decks between battles.

“Clash Royale has earned its place as a leading mobile strategy game by challenging players to think tactically, adapt, and outsmart their opponents,” said Andrea Fasulo, head of licensing at Supercell. “With The Grand Arena, our ambition is to honour that competitive spirit and strategic depth, giving fans a fresh challenge worthy of the game they love.”

highlights.title: Champions Cup: Munster beat Racing on day of Foley tributes as Saracens, Bath lose
highlights.summary: A decade to the day since the rugby world learned of head coach Anthony Foley’s death at the age of 42, Munster marked the poignant anniversary with a stirring 33-25 Champions Cup victory over Racing 92.
body: The night of Friday October 16, 2016 saw Foley pass away in his sleep the night before Munster were due to face Racing in Paris, with their fixture 10 years on staged at Páirc Uí Chaoimh in Cork.

Munster crossed for five tries in a hard-fought contest, with No 8 Brian Gleeson, wearing 24 as Foley's retired No 8 was once again taken out of circulation, joined on the scoresheet by wing Shay McCarthy, lock Tadhg Beirne, replacement Fineen Wycherley and scrum-half Craig Casey.

Racing responded with three tries of their own through wing Wilfried Hulleu, replacement scrum-half Maxime Machenaud and full-back Geronimo Prisciantelli, denying Munster a bonus-point victory. Under the tournament's new rules, teams must score at least three more tries than their opponents to secure the full five points.

The match came a day after the shocking death of Lions second row Hyron Andrews in France ahead of a Champions Cup fixture in La Rochelle. Emotional tributes were paid to both Andrews and Foley before kick-off.

highlights.title: Meta removes language that may have allowed it to scrape news sites
highlights.summary: After backlash, Meta is updating its terms again to remove language that suggested it could scrape content from sites, including news sites, to train its AI. Specifically, the following language no longer appears on the commercial terms page: … Meta may use any content from such domains, web pages…
body: Language that experts say allowed the scraping of news sites to train its AI has been removed from Meta’s terms.

Many, including Neiman Lab and James Grimmelmann, a professor of digital and information law at Cornell, interpreted it as an attempt to give Meta the right to use content scraped from sites to train its AI products for free and supersede blocking instructions in a site’s robots.txt file.

“We’ve heard you and want to clarify: the crawling terms we consolidated only applied to our ads and business products, and we’ve clarified that in the terms themselves. It does not change how Meta uses web crawlers. As always, content owners can use robots.txt to signal their preferences. This is not about scraping news sites, and these updates don’t give us new rights that supersede those preferences.”

highlights.title: James Cameron Congratulates Marvel After Avengers: Endgame Beats Avatar at the Box Office Yet Again
highlights.summary: James Cameron celebrated Avengers: Endgame beating Avatar at the box office with another social media post after the two movies traded places yet again. The director behind the smash-hit sci-fi franchise brought Iron Man to the world of Pandora with an image he shared on Instagram today.
body: "'You are one of the people,'" the post, accompanied by a picture of Iron Man surrounded by Na'vi, said. "Congratulations to Marvel and the #1 Avengers: Endgame: Encore for bringing moviegoers to the cinemas – Jim Cameron."

It's more friendly competition in the movie space that is only the latest update in a race that has seen Avatar and Avengers: Endgame trading titles for years. Marvel originally overtook Avatar's record as the highest-grossing movie in the world when it released in 2019. Cameron shared a similarly congratulatory post at the time but later went on to predict that Avatar would reclaim the throne just a few months later. He was proven right in 2021.

As Avatar sequels The Way of Water and Fire and Ash came and went, so too did more Marvel Cinematic Universe movies. As Marvel prepared for the release of its new team-up movie, Avengers: Doomsday, this December, it saw an opportunity to revisit the events of Endgame with new bonus footage, thrusting it into the future by revisiting the past.

highlights.title: How Australia’s tipping culture got awkward – and what to do about it
highlights.summary: Ten per cent, 20%, 25%? If you’ve made a cashless payment at a cafe or pub lately there’s a reasonable chance you’ve been prompted to tip. Isabella Lee looks into the arrival of US-style tip requests and where that money really goes.
body: Alyx: You’ve been thinking about tipping for a few months now, and wrote about it this week. What first sparked your interest? Isabella: I came across a post in a bartenders’ Facebook group from someone asking if their experience of having tips withheld was normal. The comments shocked me! There were more than 30 responses, with the majority of them calling out venues where they’d also been denied their tips. It made me think, if this practice was so common, why hadn’t anything been done about it?

Alyx: When you did some more digging, what did you find out? Isabella: I reached out to Fair Work to ask what legislation there was around paying out tips to staff. They told me there is none. So the original poster hadn’t experienced wage theft because the employers weren’t actually breaking any rules. It’s not just management who can dip their hand in the tip jar. Cashless payment systems take a percentage from every transaction made too. It’s pretty cheeky that the systems that allow a business to ask for tips – which changes customers’ decision-making behaviour – also get a cut.

highlights.title: Mercedes-AMG’s first ground-up SUV is a 1,150hp electric beast
highlights.summary: Earlier this year, Mercedes' AMG performance brand grabbed our attention with the GT four-door coupe, a souped-up sports sedan with three axial flux motors delivering over 1,150 horsepower.
body: It may even out-muscle the Porsche Cayenne Turbo Electric and Lucid Gravity.

The AMG GT SUV (say that five times fast) marks the first time in the performance brand’s 59-year history that it has developed a full-size SUV entirely in-house from the ground up. Scheduled to hit the US next summer, the new EV is built on Merc’s high-performance AMG.EA architecture to combine sports-car handling with full-size SUV suburban practicality.

It will be available in three trims — GT 53, GT 55, and the flagship GT 63 — with the top model delivering 1,153hp via the same three axial flux motors powering the four-door coupe. That beats the Porsche Cayenne Turbo Electric with Launch Control, which is sure to make for some awkward run-ins around Stuttgart.

Thanks to an 800-volt architecture, the SUV supports blistering-fast charging speeds up to 710kW on the 128kWh battery (GT 63 / GT 55) and 600kW on the 106kWh battery (GT 53). Drivers can charge 10–80 percent in 12 minutes or gain up to 450km (around 280 miles) of WLTP range in just 10 minutes. The 128kWh battery trims will have an estimated max range of 435 miles.

highlights.title: 5 Years Later, One Game’s Blood Sacrifice Mechanic Still Haunts Me
highlights.summary: Typically, when you’re playing a card game, the stakes aren’t that high. Perhaps you’ve got some money on the line. Maybe bragging rights are on the table. But even if you lose, largely speaking, things are going to be fine.
body: So is your host. Leshy, the forest-dwelling hermit across the table, makes his living photographing animals with a magic camera and turning their essences into playing cards. To get out, you’re going to have to beat Leshy at his own game. Just make sure he doesn’t turn you into a card before you figure out a way to escape.

In the first act of Inscryption, you’re playing a tabletop card battler against Leshy, one match at a time. Each creature card has an attack and a health stat. You place your cards in lanes across from his. Determine your play, ring a bell, and your chosen cards attack. Any creature nobody’s blocking deals damage, tracked as teeth on an ominous nearby scale. Earn five teeth, and you win the round. Each card you’d want to play has a price: Blood, usually.

highlights.title: The moment I knew: For Valentine’s Day he gave me a heart covered in fake blood. I was appalled – and thrilled
highlights.summary: Will Huxley thought Garrett looked like a Heathcliff type. They bonded over their shared love of Kate Bush. Then one day Garrett handed over an ornate gift box. Find more stories from the moment I knew series.
body: I n 2006 I’d just graduated film school at the Victorian College of the Arts and was working at the ABC in Melbourne. It was a pretty tumultuous time of my life. I had just broken up with my best friend and high school sweetheart – whom I adored – and was in the process of coming out.

I was drinking too much and in breaks from the chaos I’d find myself drawn to the local video store. That’s where I first saw Garrett behind the counter. I had an instant crush on him and spent a lot of time perusing the art house section, so he would see how creative and cultured I was.
I never had the guts to talk to him but one night in spring we ran into each other at a party. We hit it off and arranged a date at a cafe in the city.

I was obsessed with Kate Bush and Wuthering Heights, and Garrett struck me as this sort of Heathcliff type; he was a dark, handsome artist with very dramatic, gothic vibes. That day we talked about art and the things that we love. I was so excited that he shared my passion for Kate Bush, and listening to Hounds of Love on repeat. We talked about John Waters and Cindy Sherman and all these artists that were really formative for us.

highlights.title: The Tesla Roadster is far from the first car to use fans for downforce
highlights.summary: Here are some of the other, older vehicles that use fans for downforce like the Tesla Roadster does.
body: Tesla demonstrated the long-awaited next-gen Roadster with some wild stunts, starting with making the car drive up a C-shaped ramp and stop in the middle of the part perpendicular to the ground. It drove slow enough and stopped long enough to make it look like it was hanging upside down. After that, the Roadster jumped off the ramp, flipped itself upright, floated a bit and landed safely on the ground.

On its website, Tesla explained that the Roadster defied gravity by using a multi-mode fan and ground sealing system that acts as a "downforce generator." It pulls air from underneath the vehicle and provides the suction needed to hold the car upside down, at any speed. The automaker says those powered fans, along with the vehicle's retractable rear wing, provide the necessary downforce, or the force that pushes a vehicle into the ground.

highlights.title: Tim Burton's 77-Minute Stop-Motion Masterpiece Is Officially Back on Streaming
highlights.summary: When it comes to beautiful, high-quality stop-motion animation, independent studio Laika is the first name that comes to mind. The studio’s hand-crafted puppetry and 3D-printing technology have brought beautiful tales to life for years, from Coraline to ParaNorman.
body: Yet as much a technical and emotional achievement as Wildwood has proven to be, you don’t need to head to your local theater to see Laika's best animated film. All you need to do is go to HBO Max, where Tim Burton ’s masterful 2005 Corpse Bride is streaming right now.

Directed by Tim Burton and Mike Johnson, Corpse Bride follows Victor Van Dort (Johnny Depp) and his arranged marriage to Victoria Everglot (Emily Watson). After a terrible rehearsal dinner, Victor heads to the woods to practice his vows. Without thinking, he says them aloud and slips his ring onto what he believes is a tree branch sticking out from the ground. But the “branch” is actually the finger of an undead bride, Emily (Helena Bonham Carter), who immediately assumes they’re engaged. Victor is soon dragged into the land of the dead, where he comes face-to-face with its inhabitants.

highlights.title: Why Britain should reject the lure of cheap – and scary – Chinese AI
highlights.summary: In the west the technology comes with at least some effort to provide security and a benign intent – not so from China. There is much to fear from artificial intelligence developed in China and handed to businesses and governments in the west almost free of charge.
body: Every month Chinese AI developers such as DeepSeek and Xiaomi dispatch the latest versions of their “open-weight” models that allow users to take the core software and use it without paying an expensive ongoing licence.
In Britain, we love cheap Chinese kit, usually setting aside any concerns about how it was made and who by.

The row over whether to allow Chinese electric cars unfettered access to British retail forecourts is a case in point. They are cheaper than other EVs sold in the UK and, consumers ask: What is not to like? These same consumers might consider how Chinese EVs are subsidised by Beijing deliberately to boost exports and, in so doing, undermine foreign domestic car industries.
It’s scary because Beijing is entering a new phase in the long march of economic development, taking the world’s second largest economy closer to making China great again.
points: In the west the technology comes with at least some effort to provide security and a benign intent – not so from China.

highlights.title: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents
highlights.summary: Autonomous agents are the hottest thing in AI. OpenAI, Meta, Google, Instinct, and others promise their agents can scour the internet on your behalf, doing anything from booking a dinner reservation and cleaning out your inbox to buying new shoes.
body: OpenAI, Meta, and Google want AI agents to do everything for you. But popular services on the web aren’t letting that happen.

In recent weeks, users of services like Meta’s Muse, xAI’s Grok, OpenAI’s Dots, and Instinct have reported blocks preventing their AI agents from performing tasks across top websites. Yelp told TechCrunch that it only allows AI agents that pay for its data licensing program, while Delta Air Lines is preventing them from booking tickets on behalf of users. JPMorgan Chase and Charles Schwab have also confirmed that they’re blocking AI agents from accessing accounts due to security concerns. Some users say sites that previously worked with their AI agent are no longer accessible, including Cars.com and Amtrak, suggesting other companies could be quietly blocking them.

body: The actor, who was cast as Slade Wilson before the comic book movie universe was rebooted with the DCU, talked about his time working with Affleck on the canned project in his new book, Bloodlines: A Memoir. Entertainment Weekly shared excerpts from the book, which said the Batman movie would have been packed with reveals – and even a death – for some of Bruce Wayne's closest allies.

Affleck's plan for his standalone Caped Crusader flick would have seen Batman primarily tangling with Deathstroke after the character was first teased in a Justice League end-credits sequence. He described the narrative as "a superhero version of David Fincher's The Game" focused on Deathstroke trying to "dismantle Batman's entire life."

This is a plot description Manganiello has shared before, but now we know that the iconic DC villain had it out for Batman because he had been led to believe that he murdered his son. Affleck's Bruce Wayne has been known to take lives in the past, but how involved he would have been with the killing of Slade's son is unclear. It sounds like that wouldn't have stopped Deathstroke from tearing Gotham apart to get revenge.

A self-confessed cardio queen in my 20s and 30s, I alternated days at the gym with dance and Hiit classes and endured long bouts on the full complement of cardio equipment. And then my body caught up with me. First it was bursitis in my knee, which my doctor called “burpee-itis” from the ridiculous amount of the exercises I was performing. “You have to listen to your body,” he lightly chided as he poked at my swollen kneecap. My knee was still keeping me from doing a ton of basic leg work including squats and lunges, so ankle weights seemed like an easy solution. After doing some research on what would fit my specific needs, I decided on Sportneer ankle weights and used them daily for a week to see if they could enhance my lower body workouts.

highlights.title: Katie Zacharia Was Linked to an AI Rare-Earths Startup. It’s Even Weirder Than It Sounds
highlights.summary: The short-lived White House press secretary was listed as an adviser to a Kristi Noem–linked company that aims to use AI for mining. Both the company and she say she never worked there.
body: Before being fired five days into her stint as White House press secretary, Katie Zacharia spent much of the day attempting to explain her past.

Throughout her brief tenure, Zacharia’s résumé was the source of much intrigue. Foremost was the fact that despite claiming to be an attorney for much of her career, she never actually passed the California bar, as she was eventually forced to admit. Another element of her professional history, WIRED reported, was a role as an affiliate marketer for Beachbody, a fitness multilevel marketing company.

WIRED has now uncovered new details of her relationship to an AI-powered rare-earth mining operation called NRED Intelligent Mining, which counts former Department of Homeland Security secretary Kristi Noem as a strategic adviser.

On June 24, NRED—then known as NovaRed Mining, a small copper-and-gold exploration company in Vancouver, Canada—issued a press release to share that Zacharia, who had left a role as a DHS spokesperson two months before, was joining the advisory board alongside Noem.

highlights.title: Ari Emanuel Pitches Brother Rahm as Centrist Democratic President and Says He Isn’t Too Worried About AI: “It Doesn’t Have Taste”
highlights.summary: In a conversation with Tina Brown in London, the super-agent discussed his memoirs, why the UFC was his hardest deal and how live sports can provide "common ground" in a politically divided world.
body: Ari Emanuel, TKO Group executive chair and CEO and executive chairman of WME Group, was in London on Saturday to discuss his memoir, entitled Roll the Calls, published by Penguin Random House. And to no one’s surprise, he didn’t hold back, including on issues like AI, politics in the age of Donald Trump — and his brother Rahm’s potential White House run.

Emanuel, who has represented the likes of Larry David, Quentin Tarantino, Denzel Washington, Billie Eilish, Martin Scorsese and Oprah Win­frey, famously also served as the inspiration for Ari Gold, portrayed by Jeremy Piven, in the TV drama Entourage. Asked about his work as the agent to big names, he said: “What I say to people is: ‘You pay me 10 percent for my opinion. You’ll listen to my opinion. You don’t want to follow it, don’t follow it! Now I have gotten fired for giving my 10 percent. I’m OK with that. I’ve re-signed the people that have fired me, a couple of them, but you’re paying me for my opinion.”

Emanuel connected that to the rise of AI. “In this day of AI, that’s more important than anything — your opinion, your taste,” he offered. “AI doesn’t have taste, and taste only comes with time and knowledge of situations.”
points: In a conversation with Tina Brown in London, the super-agent discussed his memoirs, why the UFC was his hardest deal and how live sports can provide "common ground" in a politically divided world.
